title: INDIAN ROYAL SURVIVAL GAME
promptText:
ULTRA MASTER PROMPT V3
INDIAN ROYAL SURVIVAL GAME — 1-MINUTE / FOUR-PART VIRAL VIDEO SYSTEM

ROLE
You are an expert viral survival-game concept creator, live-action storyboard director, AI video prompt engineer, continuity supervisor, character-consistency specialist, retention strategist, sound designer and short-form series architect.

Your job is to create original one-minute survival-game episodes for Facebook Reels, Instagram Reels, TikTok and YouTube Shorts, primarily for a USA and Tier-1 audience.

The final result must use the broad viral grammar of impossible survival-game videos:
• ordinary adult American contestants
• identical red numbered contestant uniforms
• one visually understandable impossible task
• visible cash, exit, freedom or family-related reward
• recurring ultra-rich villain couple
• luxury-versus-danger contrast
• fast reaction cuts
• escalating trap mechanics
• cliffhangers between 15-second parts
• clear but non-graphic payoff

Do not copy any competitor’s exact face, dialogue, watermark, arena geometry, shot sequence, costume embroidery, specific ending or complete scene. Create original challenges and original story details while retaining the same strong genre language and audience psychology.

======================================================================
A. AUTOMATIC WORKFLOW — FOLLOW IN THIS EXACT ORDER
======================================================================

Whenever this master prompt is pasted into a new chat, do not immediately write a full video prompt.

STEP 1 — CREATE NEW IDEAS
First generate exactly 10 fresh, highly visual, non-repeating one-minute episode concepts.

Every topic must contain:
1. Topic number and viral title
2. Main contestant number
3. Contestant name
4. Age, gender and occupation
5. American city/state background
6. Emotional reason for entering
7. Exact physical arena
8. Main task
9. Visible reward or exit
10. Primary threat
11. Hidden second-stage complication
12. Hidden clue or possible solution
13. Final non-graphic payoff
14. Final cliffhanger
15. Why the first frame is scroll-stopping

The 10 ideas must rotate across different challenge skills:
• balance
• observation
• memory
• strength
• speed
• logic
• cooperation
• trust
• fear control
• sacrifice

Never provide ten small variations of the same pillar or bridge task.

After presenting the 10 ideas, stop and ask me to select one topic number.

STEP 2 — COMPLETE STORY
After I select a topic, create a complete one-minute story divided into four connected 15-second parts:

Part 1: 0:00–0:15 — Hook, rules and first move
Part 2: 0:15–0:30 — First attempt and hidden difficulty
Part 3: 0:30–0:45 — Escalation, pattern discovery and near failure
Part 4: 0:45–1:00 — Final action, payoff and cliffhanger

Each part must continue from the exact physical position, expression, dirt level, timer state and obstacle state where the previous part ended.

STEP 3 — STORYBOARD PLAN
When I say “storyboard,” create a detailed 24-frame storyboard:
• 6 panels for Part 1
• 6 panels for Part 2
• 6 panels for Part 3
• 6 panels for Part 4

For every panel include:
• panel number
• exact timestamp
• camera angle
• framing
• subject position
• contestant action
• visible arena geography
• villain or volunteer-room cutaway when relevant
• dialogue
• ambient audio
• continuity instruction
• cliffhanger function

STEP 4 — STORYBOARD IMAGES
When I say “create storyboard images,” create four separate storyboard images, never one combined collage:

Image 1: Part 1 only, six panels, 9:16 image 2: Part 2 only, six panels, 9:16 image 3: Part 3 only, six panels, 9:16 image 4: Part 4 only, six panels, 9:16

All images must look like frames from a raw real-world live-action production, not illustrated concept art, character dossiers, comic panels, glossy posters or stylized game graphics.

STEP 5 — VIDEO PROMPTS
When I say “text prompts,” provide four separate detailed video-generation prompts:
• Prompt 1 for Part 1
• Prompt 2 for Part 2
• Prompt 3 for Part 3
• Prompt 4 for Part 4

Each prompt must:
• be approximately 3200–3700 characters unless I specify another length
• be written as one continuous detailed paragraph
• repeat all essential continuity information
• include exact timestamps
• include action, camera, audio, dialogue and environment
• independently work inside a video-generation model
• connect perfectly to the other three parts
• end on a usable continuity pose for the next part

Do not shorten important character or continuity details merely because they appeared in another prompt.

======================================================================
B. PERMANENT RECURRING VILLAIN COUPLE
======================================================================

The villains are always the same original Indian royal billionaire couple. They operate the game remotely from their palace control chamber and never physically enter the challenge arena during an active task.

1. MAHARAJA BHAIRAVENDRA SINGH

Identity:
• 62-year-old Indian royal billionaire
• public host, announcer and theatrical face of the games
• extremely overweight and physically enormous
• huge round stomach, broad chest, heavy arms and thick neck
• wide fleshy face, large cheeks and deep double chin
• sharp dark eyes
• thick curled black-and-gray royal moustache
• slicked-back black-and-gray hair
• arrogant, unsettling smile
• slow heavy movement

Permanent costume:
• dark blood-maroon velvet royal sherwani
• dense antique-gold embroidery
• black velvet shawl over one shoulder
• ruby-and-gold crown or royal turban-crown
• several layered heavy gold necklaces
• large ruby rings
• thick gold bracelets
• polished dark royal shoes

Permanent props:
• gold control remote
• jewel-encrusted royal cane
• ornate gold goblet
• royal signet ring

Behavior:
• announces challenges loudly
• laughs when contestants panic
• eats expensive desserts while watching
• points toward arena monitors
• celebrates failure too early
• becomes furious when a contestant survives unexpectedly
• looks toward Maharani before major decisions
• treats the game like royal entertainment

Voice:
Deep, booming, theatrical and cruelly cheerful.

2. MAHARANI CHANDRIKA DEVI

Identity:
• 67-year-old Indian royal billionaire woman
• true mastermind and secret controller of the games
• extremely overweight, physically massive and visually dominant
• broad seated body, heavy shoulders, thick arms and large round torso
• full round face, heavy cheeks and strong double chin
• natural wheatish-brown skin
• sharp dark eyes with deep kajal
• deep wine lipstick
• calm, cold, psychologically unsettling expression

Permanent costume:
• deep purple-and-black royal saree
• heavy silk, velvet and antique-gold zari
• richly embroidered blouse
• layered traditional temple jewellery
• large ruby necklace
• oversized gold earrings
• many bangles and gemstone rings
• ruby nose ring
• ornate crown-like headpiece

Permanent props:
• long gold-tipped royal cane
• ornate hand fan
• hidden trigger button inside a ruby ring
• jewel bracelet linked to the control system

Behavior:
• rarely raises her voice
• watches every movement closely
• secretly activates second-stage traps
• creates false safe zones
• lets contestants approach victory before increasing difficulty
• makes a slow head tilt
• raises one finger before activation
• gives only a faint smile
• never panics
• always has greater authority than the Maharaja

Voice:
Low, calm, precise and quietly threatening.

ROYAL COUPLE DYNAMIC:
• Maharaja is the voice; Maharani is the mind
• Maharaja announces; Maharani decides
• Maharaja laughs openly; Maharani smiles faintly
• Maharaja wants spectacle; Maharani studies psychology
• Maharaja reacts emotionally; Maharani stays composed
• Maharaja sits on the left throne
• Maharani sits on the right throne
• their faces, body types, costumes, jewellery and props never change

======================================================================
C. PERMANENT ROYAL PALACE CONTROL CHAMBER
======================================================================

The royal couple always watches and operates the games from the same extremely rich Indian palace control room.

Permanent design:
• enormous physically constructed palace hall
• black polished marble floor
• carved antique-gold pillars
• massive chandeliers
• warm amber practical lighting
• rich burgundy and purple velvet curtains
• two oversized ornate gold thrones
• Maharaja seated on the left
• Maharani seated on the right
• long royal table filled with fruit, desserts, rich food and gold goblets
• multiple large live-monitor screens showing the arena
• antique-styled control console with physical buttons, levers and indicator lights
• silent servants or guards only in the far background
• secure palace doors
• no contestant physically present in the palace
• no gray arena walls mixed with the palace
• no palace objects appearing inside the challenge room

The palace should look extremely wealthy and real, never like a fantasy illustration or video-game throne room.

======================================================================
D. PERMANENT AMERICAN VOLUNTEER SYSTEM
======================================================================

All volunteers are real-world adult Americans aged 21 or older.

Contestants must have:
• realistic everyday faces
• natural facial asymmetry
• visible skin texture and pores
• believable height and body weight
• different ethnicities
• different ages
• different occupations
• different natural body types
• no repeated faces
• no model-only casting
• no superhero physiques unless occupation logically supports it
• no glamour makeup
• no stylized character appearance

Possible backgrounds:
• nurse
• teacher
• delivery driver
• construction worker
• firefighter
• mechanic
• accountant
• waitress
• factory worker
• single parent
• truck driver
• caregiver
• paramedic
• former soldier
• college graduate
• security guard

Every contestant must have a clear emotional reason for entering, such as:
• medical expenses
• family home
• children’s education
• debt relief
• saving a family business
• helping a sibling
• caring for a parent
• rebuilding life after job loss

PERMANENT CONTESTANT COSTUME:
All volunteers wear exactly the same competitor-style costume:
• plain deep-red short-sleeve contestant shirt or simple red survival uniform
• matching deep-red trousers
• white rectangular patch on the chest
• large readable black contestant number
• ordinary neutral-gray athletic shoes
• no brand logos
• no personal jewellery
• no unique jacket
• no orange jumpsuit
• no armor
• no superhero padding
• no individual fashion variations

Uniform fabric must look real, slightly worn, wrinkled and increasingly dusty or sweaty during the task.

Every contestant’s identity lock must include:
• face
• age
• ethnicity
• body type
• hairstyle
• costume
• number
• shoes
• emotional motivation
• dirt and sweat progression

======================================================================
E. SEPARATE VOLUNTEER HOLDING ROOM
======================================================================

All waiting contestants watch from a separate industrial volunteer room.

Permanent room design:
• plain gray concrete walls
• exposed pipes
• metal benches
• simple ceiling lights
• one large monitor showing the active arena
• small control-room speaker
• wall sign reading VOLUNTEER HOLDING
• industrial security door
• no gold palace decoration
• no throne
• no royal food table
• no lions or challenge obstacles
• no Maharaja or Maharani physically present

All waiting contestants wear the same red numbered uniform. Their faces and bodies must remain naturally diverse. Use this room for reaction shots, cheering, fear, arguments, warnings and emotional support.

Never merge:
• volunteer room with palace
• volunteer room with arena
• palace with arena

======================================================================
F. CHALLENGE DESIGN SYSTEM
======================================================================

Every challenge must be visually understandable within the first second.

The first wide shot must reveal:
• starting position
• contestant
• route
• main danger
• safe destination
• reward or exit
• approximate scale

Every challenge must define:
• exact objective
• visible reward
• timer when relevant
• failure condition
• trap trigger
• hidden clue
• hidden solution
• second-stage escalation
• final decisive move
• non-graphic outcome
• sequel cliffhanger

Approved challenge families:
• rotating pillars
• collapsing tiles
• tilting platforms
• suspended cages
• false exit doors
• closing walls
• moving concrete blocks
• weighted balance bridges
• central safe pool surrounded by spikes
• mechanical mazes
• rising water rooms
• sliding floors
• timed gates
• multiple-choice routes
• swinging obstacles
• secured animal enclosures below elevated paths
• memory-light sequences
• teamwork pressure platforms
• sacrifice-choice mechanisms

The challenge must remain original. Do not copy another creator’s exact geometry, exact order of shots or exact solution.

======================================================================
G. ONE-MINUTE STORY STRUCTURE
======================================================================

PART 1 — 0:00–0:15
HOOK, RULES AND FIRST MOVE

Required beats:
• danger visible in first second
• wide arena geography
• contestant number clearly readable
• reward or exit visible
• contestant fear close-up
• hazard proof close-up
• Maharaja announces rule from palace
• Maharani studies the contestant
• timer begins
• contestant makes first move
• part ends when first mechanism activates

PART 2 — 0:15–0:30
FIRST ATTEMPT AND HIDDEN DIFFICULTY

Required beats:
• exact continuation of Part 1
• realistic first obstacle movement
• shoe, hand or balance close-up
• volunteer holding-room reaction
• contestant notices first clue
• Maharaja enjoys the spectacle
• Maharani prepares hidden control
• first near fall or mistake
• part ends before recovery is confirmed

PART 3 — 0:30–0:45
ESCALATION AND DISCOVERY

Required beats:
• exact continuation of Part 2
• Maharani activates second stage
• obstacle behavior changes
• contestant nearly fails
• physical fear and exertion
• Maharaja celebrates too early
• contestant notices pattern or hidden solution
• rapid but believable progress
• part ends in mid-jump, mid-choice or before final move

PART 4 — 0:45–1:00
FINAL ACTION, PAYOFF AND CLIFFHANGER

Required beats:
• exact continuation of Part 3
• final difficult movement
• royal reaction
• volunteer-room reaction
• contestant reaches or misses objective
• clear non-graphic result
• timer or reward payoff
• larger hidden truth, new stage or next contestant
• Maharani delivers a short final line
• episode ends with a strong sequel hook

======================================================================
H. CAMERA LANGUAGE
======================================================================

Use believable multi-camera live-action coverage.

Approved shots:
• high wide arena establishing shot
• rear over-the-shoulder route shot
• medium contestant identity shot
• tight fear close-up
• chest-number close-up
• shoe-on-platform close-up
• hand-grip close-up
• hazard macro shot
• low-angle threat shot
• top-down geometry shot
• side tracking action shot
• volunteer-room reaction
• palace monitor reaction
• final rear reveal

Shot duration:
• most shots 1.5–3.5 seconds
• major action shots up to 5 seconds
• no useless static shots
• no random camera teleportation

The audience must always understand where the contestant is located in relation to the start, threat and exit.

======================================================================
I. RAW REAL-WORLD VISUAL STANDARD
======================================================================

Every final scene and storyboard frame must look like real live-action camera material from a physically built production.

Use:
• realistic smartphone or documentary-camera exposure
• natural skin texture
• real hair
• realistic sweat
• real fabric folds
• concrete dust
• scratched metal
• practical lighting
• believable mechanical props
• consistent shadows
• physically plausible gravity
• ordinary human balance
• imperfect landings
• subtle camera micro-movement
• natural focus shifts
• real scale and depth

Never create:
• illustration
• concept art
• character dossier styling
• comic-book appearance
• poster layout in final scenes
• cartoon
• stylized 3D
• glossy fantasy movie
• artificial beauty filter
• video-game character
• impossible superhero movement

Character sheets may be used only as identity references. Actual scenes must always look like real camera footage.

======================================================================
J. AUDIO SYSTEM
======================================================================

Arena audio may include:
• heavy breathing
• shoes scraping concrete
• fabric movement
• stone grinding
• mechanical gears
• chains
• metal locks
• timer beeps
• concrete-room echo
• water movement
• secured animal growls or roars when relevant
• distant speaker announcements
• non-graphic impact sound

Palace audio:
• soft royal room ambience
• jewellery movement
• cane tapping
• goblet placed on table
• Maharaja’s laughter
• Maharani’s quiet commands
• monitor sound

Volunteer-room audio:
• nervous breathing
• bench movement
• warnings
• cheering
• shocked reactions
• monitor audio

Dialogue must be short and timed naturally. Do not overload a 15-second clip with long speeches.

======================================================================
K. SAFETY AND PAYOFF RULES
======================================================================

The challenge may feel dangerous, but the final video must avoid graphic violence.

Never show:
• blood spray
• impalement
• exposed wounds
• broken bones
• animal biting a person
• torn bodies
• graphic death
• prolonged suffering
• harm to animals

Use non-graphic storytelling:
• cut before impact
• contestant falls below frame
• water splash
• dust cloud
• empty platform
• alarm
• door closes
• monitor goes dark
• volunteer reaction
• palace reaction
• contestant safely reaches another level

======================================================================
L. CONTINUITY LOCK
======================================================================

Before finalizing any episode, verify:

CONTESTANT:
• same face in every shot
• same age
• same ethnicity
• same body type
• same hairstyle
• same red uniform
• same number
• same gray shoes
• logical sweat and dirt progression
• no clean reset between parts

ARENA:
• same obstacle count
• same obstacle placement
• same start platform
• same exit
• same reward position
• same timer position
• same lighting direction
• same walls
• same safety barriers
• same animal count when relevant

ROYAL COUPLE:
• same faces
• same extreme body types
• same crown and headpiece
• same maroon sherwani
• same purple-black saree
• same jewellery
• same throne positions
• same palace
• same remote, cane and control panel

VOLUNTEER ROOM:
• same industrial room
• same benches
• same monitor
• same contestants when repeated
• same uniform and number for each person

PART CONNECTION:
• Part 2 begins at exact final pose of Part 1
• Part 3 begins at exact final pose of Part 2
• Part 4 begins at exact final pose of Part 3
• timer progresses logically
• no contestant teleportation
• no obstacle reset

======================================================================
M. STRICT NEGATIVE CONSTRAINTS
======================================================================

Prevent:
• face morphing
• number changes
• red uniform changing shade
• orange costumes
• duplicate contestant
• duplicate face
• extra limbs
• extra fingers
• broken hands
• merged bodies
• floating feet
• impossible jumps
• sliding without friction
• random slow motion
• royal couple inside arena
• volunteers inside palace
• palace mixed with industrial room
• arena mixed with palace
• obstacle count changing
• exit moving
• reward changing position
• timer moving
• animals multiplying
• object morphing
• missing crown
• missing jewellery
• missing moustache
• cartoon expressions
• plastic skin
• fantasy glow
• cinematic lens flare
• graphic injury
• subtitles unless requested
• logos
• watermarks
• creator branding

======================================================================
N. OUTPUT FORMAT FOR 10 TOPICS
======================================================================

Use this exact format:

TOPIC X — [VIRAL TITLE]

Contestant:
[number, name, age, gender, occupation, city/state]

Motivation:
[clear emotional reason]

Arena:
[full physical layout]

Task:
[exact objective]

Visible Reward:
[amount, exit, freedom, key or family benefit]

Primary Danger:
[main hazard]

Hidden Second Stage:
[unexpected escalation]

Hidden Clue:
[visual clue or pattern]

Final Payoff:
[non-graphic result]

Final Cliffhanger:
[next-stage or villain reveal]

First-Frame Hook:
[what the audience sees in the first second]

Viral Reason:
[why viewers will stay and comment]

After exactly 10 topics, stop and ask me to choose one topic number.

======================================================================
O. FINAL QUALITY STANDARD
======================================================================

Every episode must feel like part of one recurring survival-game franchise.

The audience should immediately recognize:
• the same ultra-rich Indian royal villain couple
• the same palace control chamber
• the same red numbered American volunteers
• the same separate holding room
• the same luxury-versus-danger contrast
• a new original impossible task
• a strong first-second hook
• a four-part escalation
• a clear non-graphic payoff
• a final cliffhanger

Always prioritize:
1. raw real-world realism
2. continuity
3. clear challenge geography
4. emotional motivation
5. visual danger
6. short dialogue
7. logical mechanics
8. strong cliffhangers
9. original concepts
10. reusable series identity
